title: Sell Mineral Rights in Rome, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Rome, PA
metaDescription: Rome, Bradford County mineral rights owner in dry-gas Marcellus country? We buy oil and gas interests, review your lease, and pay a fair cash price.
heroLead: Rome sits in Bradford County along the Susquehanna's North Branch, one of the highest-producing dry-gas counties in the entire Marcellus play, and families here have generally had no shortage of drilling activity to watch over the past decade and a half.
intro: Bradford County was one of the counties that got hit hardest and fastest by early Marcellus leasing, and Rome-area landowners often signed leases in the middle of that rush, sometimes without a lot of time to compare terms across offers. If you're still holding that original lease, or an interest that's been passed down since, we can tell you plainly what it's worth today.

sections.heading: One of the State's Top-Producing Counties
paragraphs: Bradford County has consistently ranked among Pennsylvania's top gas-producing counties since the boom began, and Rome sits well within that productive footprint. That history gives us strong data to work from — actual production and royalty trends from nearby units rather than a rough estimate.

Some of the larger operators that built big acreage positions here have shifted their focus or reduced activity over the years, which has left some Rome-area leases in a kind of holding pattern. We can explain what that means for your specific interest based on its current status.

sections.heading: What a Bradford County Deduction Fight Looks Like
paragraphs: We've talked with Rome families frustrated by royalty statements that don't match what they expected based on gross production numbers, a common story across Bradford County given how many leases here were signed before Pennsylvania courts clarified how post-production deductions could be applied. We'll break down your statement with you and tell you honestly whether it looks in line with what we see elsewhere.

faqs.question: Is Rome still an active area for gas drilling?
faqs.answer: Bradford County remains one of the top-producing counties in the state, though activity has shifted over time. We check current status for your specific unit.

faqs.question: My lease is over ten years old. Is it still valid?
faqs.answer: Many leases from the boom years remain in effect through held-by-production clauses if a well is actively producing. We review your lease terms as part of our offer.

faqs.question: Can you help me understand why my royalty dropped over the years?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's typically normal production decline combined with post-production deductions, and we'll walk through your statement with you.

faqs.question: What if the operator on my lease has changed hands since it was signed?
faqs.answer: That's common in Bradford County as companies have bought and sold acreage positions over the years. We trace the current operator of record before making an offer.
